flagged.evidence: The Statement assumes only that transition-density integrals “can be differentiated in time” and their resulting derivatives “are integrable.” Step 1.2 says domination makes the local remainder divided by h tend to zero; step 2.1 says “the stated domination permits” the partition sums to converge. No local or time-uniform bound or integrable majorant is stated. The cited dominated-convergence theorem requires a single integrable majorant for the sequence, and the Fubini theorem requires an L1 function on the product space; neither licenses these limits. The finite-time generator identity and martingale problem therefore do not follow from the stated hypotheses.
